MSCI 101.description: Origin and evolution of the oceans, plate tectonics, ocean circulation, waves and tides, seawater and sediment composition, and influences on biology. Three lecture and three laboratory hours per week. Scheduled field trips required.
MSCI 101.subject: MSCI
MSCI 101.title: The Ocean Environment

MSCI 102.description: Origin, evolution, and diversity of marine life, biological production, trophic dynamics, nutrient cycles, marine resources, and environmental concerns. Three lecture and three laboratory hours per week. Scheduled field trips required.
MSCI 102.subject: MSCI
MSCI 102.title: The Living Ocean

MSCI 210.description: A nontechnical introduction to human interactions with the marine environment: marine organisms, marine systems, and the physical and chemical characteristics of oceans and estuaries. Not available for marine science major credit.
MSCI 210.subject: MSCI
MSCI 210.title: Oceans and Society

MSCI 210L.description: Experiments and exercises which illustrate how specific components of marine environments are structured, function, and can be measured. Two laboratory hours per week. Not available for marine science major credit. Attendance on designated field trips may be required.
MSCI 210L.subject: MSCI
MSCI 210L.title: Oceans and Society Laboratory

MSCI 215.description: Coastal zones of South Carolina and neighboring states, including geologic history, geomorphology, stratigraphy, hydrogeology, shoreline processes, environmental issues, and effects of man. Not available for geological science or marine science major credit. Three lecture hours each week plus optional field trips.
MSCI 215.subject: MSCI
MSCI 215.title: Coastal Environments of the Southeastern U.S.

MSCI 215L.description: Exercises examining coastal ecology, geomorphology, hydrogeology, shoreline processes, environmental issues, and human impact. Not available for marine science major credit. Two laboratory hours per week. Scheduled field trips required.
MSCI 215L.subject: MSCI
MSCI 215L.title: Coastal Environments of the Southeastern U.S. (Laboratory)

MSCI 305.description: Instrumentation, oceanographic time series, spatial and directional data sets, and basic parametric modeling.
MSCI 305.subject: MSCI
MSCI 305.title: Ocean Data Analysis

MSCI 311.description: Biological concepts emphasizing adaptation to marine environments. Laboratory experiments emphasize principles and techniques of marine biological study. Three lecture and three laboratory hours per week. Scheduled field trips are required.
MSCI 311.subject: MSCI
MSCI 311.title: Biology of Marine Organisms

MSCI 313.description: Biogeochemical cycling, carbonate chemistry, climate change, hydrothermal vents, stable isotopes, trace metals, radioactive tracers, mass balance, and properties of sea water. Three lecture and three laboratory hours per week.
MSCI 313.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in MSCI 101, CHEM 111, CHEM 112, and MATH 141.
MSCI 313.subject: MSCI
MSCI 313.title: The Chemistry of the Sea

MSCI 314.description: Properties of seawater, mass and momentum balances, circulation, mixing, waves and other processes in the marine environment.
MSCI 314.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in MSCI 101 and MATH 141; C or better in PHYS 201 or PHYS 211.
MSCI 314.subject: MSCI
MSCI 314.title: Physical Oceanography

MSCI 316.description: An exploration of the science behind oil spills, toxic chemicals, microplastics, and other organic pollutants impacting our oceans, from coastlines to the deep-sea. Emphasis on how these contaminants move, transform, and affect marine life and human health, and how cutting-edge science drives legal action and policy change.
MSCI 316.subject: MSCI
MSCI 316.title: Marine Organic Pollution

MSCI 335.description: The science of global change, its relation to the hydrosphere, atmosphere, lithosphere, and biosphere. Global system science, biogeochemical cycles, paleoclimatology, glaciation, and eustacy.
MSCI 335.subject: MSCI
MSCI 335.title: Processes of Global Environmental Change

MSCI 360.description: Exploration of post-graduation opportunities in academia and industry. Interactive discussion of topics including helping skills, active listening, oral communication, goal setting, interviewing, and building a strong professional portfolio.
MSCI 360.subject: MSCI
MSCI 360.title: SEOE Peer Mentorship, Leadership, Professional Development

MSCI 365.description: Computational analysis of earth, marine, and environmental datasets applying time series analysis, regression, filtering, and statistical analysis.
MSCI 365.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in CSCE 106 or higher; C or better in MATH 122 or higher.
MSCI 365.subject: MSCI
MSCI 365.title: Data Science in Earth, Ocean and Environmental Science

MSCI 375.description: The Deep Sea is an interdisciplinary, scientific survey of the geology, biology, chemistry, and physical setting of the deep-sea (more than 1000 m depth).
MSCI 375.subject: MSCI
MSCI 375.title: The Deep Sea

MSCI 390.description: Analysis of past and current issues in global and national marine policy. Relationship between science and policymakers.
MSCI 390.subject: MSCI
MSCI 390.title: Policy and Marine Science

MSCI 399.description: Contract approved by instructor, advisor, and department chair is required for undergraduate students.
MSCI 399.subject: MSCI
MSCI 399.title: Independent Study

MSCI 450.description: Principles and methods of measuring production in the sea. Emphasis on the ocean’s role in the global carbon budget. Three lecture hours per week. Scheduled field trips are required.
MSCI 450.subject: MSCI
MSCI 450.title: Principles of Biological Oceanography

MSCI 460.description: Intensive inquiry-based investigations combining oceanographic field sampling with laboratory measurements of collected samples using modern analytical instrumentation, and with analysis and integration of data into a final research report. Most of the course is conducted in residence at a marine field site.
MSCI 460.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in MSCI 101 and MSCI 102 or C or better in BIOL 101 and 102.
MSCI 460.subject: MSCI
MSCI 460.title: Field and Laboratory Investigations in Marine Science

MSCI 495.description: Internship experience that offers practical field or laboratory experience in oceanography and/or related marine sciences. Course content varies and will be announced by title in schedule of courses. Usually conducted off campus and student must be able to access internship on their own.
MSCI 495.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in MSCI 311, MSCI 313 and MSCI 314.
MSCI 495.subject: MSCI
MSCI 495.title: Internship in Marine Science

MSCI 496.description: Student research on problems of fundamental significance in collaboration with faculty mentors. Emphasis on critical thinking, problem solving, proposal development, scientific writing, and professional presentation. Nine hours of laboratory, field, or library work per week.
MSCI 496.subject: MSCI
MSCI 496.title: Undergraduate Research

MSCI 497.description: Student research on problems of fundamental significance in collaboration with faculty mentors. Emphasis on critical thinking, problem solving, proposal development, scientific writing, and professional presentation. Nine hours of laboratory, field, or library work per week.
MSCI 497.subject: MSCI
MSCI 497.title: Undergraduate Research

MSCI 498.description: Student research on problems of fundamental significance in collaboration with faculty mentors. Emphasis on critical thinking, problem solving, proposal development, scientific writing, and professional presentation. Nine hours of laboratory, field, or library work per week.
MSCI 498.subject: MSCI
MSCI 498.title: Undergraduate Research

MSCI 499.description: Student research on problems of fundamental significance in collaboration with faculty mentors. Emphasis on critical thinking, problem solving, proposal development, scientific writing, and professional presentation. Nine hours of laboratory, field, or library work per week.
MSCI 499.subject: MSCI
MSCI 499.title: Undergraduate Research

MSCI 501.description: The process of earth denudation with emphasis on chemistry of weathering, stream and erosion hydraulics, quantitative analysis of land form evolution.
MSCI 501.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in GEOL 101.
MSCI 501.subject: MSCI
MSCI 501.title: Principles of Geomorphology

MSCI 502.description: Geological and physical controls on the morphology, development, and stability of coastlines. Analysis of waves and erosional processes, and coastal zone morphodynamics. Several required field trips.
MSCI 502.subject: MSCI
MSCI 502.title: Principles of Coastal Geomorphology

MSCI 503.description: An overview of the microbial world including a survey of the distribution, functioning, and diversity of microorganisms in natural systems. Discusses the crucial roles that microorganisms play in ecosystem function, biogeochemical cycles, and environmental quality.
MSCI 503.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in MSCI 102 or BIOL 102; C or better in CHEM 112.
MSCI 503.subject: MSCI
MSCI 503.title: Environmental Microbiology

MSCI 504.description: This course will discuss the urgent need for deploying solar radiation and carbon dioxide removal approaches at scale, including potential benefits and risks of these options. It will also discuss regulatory and governance considerations at both the national and international level and strategizes to incentivize large-scale adoption of these approaches.
MSCI 504.subject: MSCI
MSCI 504.title: Climate Geoengineering

MSCI 506.description: Application of the principles of ecology with the methods of engineering to design sustainable ecosystems to better integrate human society with the coastal environment.
MSCI 506.subject: MSCI
MSCI 506.title: Coastal Nature-Based Solutions

MSCI 509.description: MATLAB-based course in processing, analysis, and visualization of large oceanographic data sets. Includes scalar and vector time series measured at fixed locations as well as shipboard surveys of oceanographic characteristics varying both in 3-D and in time. Methods and techniques are relevant to other geoscience disciplines.
MSCI 509.subject: MSCI
MSCI 509.title: MATLAB-Based Data Analysis in Ocean Sciences

MSCI 510.description: Phylogenetic and comparative aspects of anatomy, physiology, reproduction, and embryology of the invertebrates. Three lecture and one three-hour laboratory period per week.
MSCI 510.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in BIOL 301 or MSCI 311.
MSCI 510.subject: MSCI
MSCI 510.title: Invertebrate Zoology

MSCI 511.description: Systematic, ecologic, biogeographic, and evolutionary aspects of paleontology; lectures, practical exercises, field trips.
MSCI 511.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in GEOL 305.
MSCI 511.subject: MSCI
MSCI 511.title: Advanced Paleontology

MSCI 515.description: Marine microfossils; distribution, ecology, paleoecology, and biostratigraphy; use of microfossils in marine sediments to study oceanographic history. Three lectures and two laboratory hours per week.
MSCI 515.subject: MSCI
MSCI 515.title: Marine Micropaleontology

MSCI 521.description: Investigation of low temperature chemical reactions controlling the geochemistry of the earth’s surface. Emphasis on CO2, carbonates, oxidation-reduction, thermodynamics, isotopes, biogeochemistry.
MSCI 521.subject: MSCI
MSCI 521.title: Introduction to Geochemistry

MSCI 524.description: Introduction to radioactivity and the use of radionuclides to study environmental processes, including age-dating and biogeochemical cycling in aquatic systems.
MSCI 524.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in CHEM 111, CHEM 112 and MATH 141.
MSCI 524.subject: MSCI
MSCI 524.title: Environmental Radioisotope Geochemistry

MSCI 525.description: Diversity, distribution, physiology, ecology, evolution, and economic importance of marine algal, seagrass, and mangrove communities. Three lecture and three laboratory hours per week. Scheduled field trips are required.
MSCI 525.subject: MSCI
MSCI 525.title: Marine Plants

MSCI 535.description: Management and conservation of aquatic and marine resources, with emphasis on fisheries. Data procurement and analysis; commercial and recreational fisheries; sociological, political, legal, and environmental factors that affect fishery management; and fish biodiversity.
MSCI 535.subject: MSCI
MSCI 535.title: Fishery Management

MSCI 536.description: Phylogeny, morphology, behavior, and ecology of fishes. Three lecture and 3 laboratory hours plus three field trips to be arranged.
MSCI 536.subject: MSCI
MSCI 536.title: Ichthyology

MSCI 537.description: Introduction to the practical and scientific aspects of the commercial culture of freshwater and marine organisms. Three lecture hours per week. One all-day field trip required.
MSCI 537.subject: MSCI
MSCI 537.title: Aquaculture

MSCI 538.description: The identification of behavioral adaptations of estuarine and marine organisms: their ecology, physiology, development, and evolutionary history; field observations.
MSCI 538.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: BIOL 101 and BIOL 102 or MSCI 311.
MSCI 538.subject: MSCI
MSCI 538.title: Behavior of Marine Organisms

MSCI 545.description: A comprehensive study of the origin and development of the major structural features of the ocean basins and the continental margins. Discussion of the techniques used in obtaining geologic data and the interpretation of sedimentary processes, vulcanism, and the stratigraphy of the ocean basins.
MSCI 545.subject: MSCI
MSCI 545.title: Geological Oceanography

MSCI 550.description: Problems of sequence stratigraphy resolved with graphic computer simulations. Sedimentary fill of basins by carbonates and/or clastics tracked as a function of rate of sediment accumulation, tectonic behavior, and sea level. Includes laboratory.
MSCI 550.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in GEOL 325.
MSCI 550.subject: MSCI
MSCI 550.title: Sedimentary Simulations and Sequence Stratigraphy

MSCI 552.description: An introduction to the principles of population genetics, with emphasis on the origin, maintenance, and significance of genetic variation in natural populations.
MSCI 552.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in BIOL 301 or MSCI 311.
MSCI 552.subject: MSCI
MSCI 552.title: Population Genetics

MSCI 553.description: Marine sedimentary environments; physical/biological factors which control the formation and distribution of modern marine sediments.
MSCI 553.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in GEOL 516.
MSCI 553.subject: MSCI
MSCI 553.title: Marine Sediments

MSCI 555.description: Introduces the field of conservation and explores the intersection between conservation and environmental health with a particular focus on coastal and marine case studies.
MSCI 555.subject: MSCI
MSCI 555.title: Conservation and Health in Marine Systems

MSCI 557.description: Physical and geological processes controlling the formation and evolution of beach, barrier, and nearshore environments, including discussion of coastal management issues.
MSCI 557.subject: MSCI
MSCI 557.title: Coastal Processes

MSCI 566.description: The formulation and simulation of compartment models of marine and terrestrial ecosystems with complex nutrient cycling, food chains, and energy flow. Analog and digital simulation techniques. Ecosystem stability and sensitivity. Organization, structure, and diversity of an ecosystem.
MSCI 566.subject: MSCI
MSCI 566.title: Ecosystem Analysis

MSCI 568.description: Small-scale processes in the atmospheric boundary layers, including energy budget, radiation, soil heat transfer, humidity, viscous flows, turbulence, momentum and heat exchanges, evaporation, and marine atmospheric boundary layer.
MSCI 568.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in PHYS 201 and MATH 141.
MSCI 568.subject: MSCI
MSCI 568.title: Introduction to Micrometeorology

MSCI 574.description: Exploration of how human activities affect marine natural populations, species, communities and ecosystems, including threats to biodiversity; approaches to marine conservation; and ecological and evolutionary responses to anthropogenic disturbance.
MSCI 574.subject: MSCI
MSCI 574.title: Marine Conservation Biology

MSCI 575.description: Structure, dynamics, and interactions between populations and communities in marine ecosystems. Attendance at designated departmental seminars is required. Three lecture hours per week.
MSCI 575.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: CHEM 111 and BIOL 301 or MSCI 311.
MSCI 575.subject: MSCI
MSCI 575.title: Marine Ecology

MSCI 575L.description: Laboratory and field exercises in coastal environments. Three hours per week plus field trips.
MSCI 575L.subject: MSCI
MSCI 575L.title: Marine Ecology Laboratory

MSCI 576.description: Interdisciplinary examination of the distribution, reproduction, survival, and historical variation of the principal commercial marine fisheries.
MSCI 576.subject: MSCI
MSCI 576.title: Marine Fisheries Ecology

MSCI 577.description: Structure, productivity, and biodiversity of coral reefs, emphasizing their sensitivity, stability, and sustainability. Taught as an extended field experience with daily lectures and guided research activities.
MSCI 577.subject: MSCI
MSCI 577.title: Ecology of Coral Reefs

MSCI 578.description: Functional adaptation of marine plants and animals to ecological stresses including pollution. Three lecture hours per week.
MSCI 578.subject: MSCI
MSCI 578.title: Physiological and Pollution Ecology of Marine Organisms

MSCI 579.description: The physical mechanism responsible for interaction between the ocean and the atmosphere and the influence of air-sea interaction on atmospheric and oceanic dynamics and thermodynamics on a wide variety of spatial/temporal scales.
MSCI 579.subject: MSCI
MSCI 579.title: Air-Sea Interaction

MSCI 580.description: This course provides knowledge of various techniques used in satellite remote sensing of the oceans. Key skills will be developed in satellite data processing, image analysis, and hands-on research.
MSCI 580.subject: MSCI
MSCI 580.title: Satellite Oceanography

MSCI 581.description: Estuarine kinematics and dynamics; classification of estuaries; estuarine circulation and mixing. Scheduled field trips are required.
MSCI 581.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in MSCI 314.
MSCI 581.subject: MSCI
MSCI 581.title: Estuarine Oceanography

MSCI 582.description: Basic principles of fluid statics and dynamics. Conservation of mass, momentum, and energy; viscosity, vorticity, and boundary layers with examples from the marine environment. Applications to and analysis of ocean currents and waves.
MSCI 582.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in MATH 241 and C or better in either PHYS 201 or PHYS 211.
MSCI 582.subject: MSCI
MSCI 582.title: Marine Hydrodynamics

MSCI 583.description: Geological and geochemical processes in salt marshes. Methods of geological research in marshes including instrumental techniques, sampling design, and data analysis. Two lectures per week plus four weekends of project oriented fieldwork and/or equivalent lab work. Scheduled field trips are required.
MSCI 583.subject: MSCI
MSCI 583.title: Geology and Geochemistry of Salt Marshes

MSCI 585.description: Descriptive oceanography of mangrove and coral reef coasts with emphasis on physical processes. Taught as an extended field experience with daily lectures and guided research activities.
MSCI 585.subject: MSCI
MSCI 585.title: Coastal Tropical Oceanography

MSCI 590.description: Influence of wind on coastal systems, with emphasis on nearshore currents, sediment transport and bedforms, aeolian transport, and dunes. Minimum Junior standing required.
MSCI 590.subject: MSCI
MSCI 590.title: Beach-Dune Interactions

MSCI 599.description: Current developments in marine science selected to meet faculty and student interests. Course content varies and will be announced by title in schedule of courses.
MSCI 599.subject: MSCI
MSCI 599.title: Topics in Marine Science

MSCI 624.description: Study of the chemical reactions and processes affecting the distribution of chemical species in natural systems. Three lecture hours per week.
MSCI 624.subject: MSCI
MSCI 624.title: Aquatic Chemistry

MSCI 627.description: Examines the physiology and ecology of phytoplankton, including environmental controls on community composition, primary productivity, and detection and characterization of water quality (eutrophication) and harmful algal blooms.
MSCI 627.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: MSCI 102 or MSCI 450 or BIOL 450.
MSCI 627.subject: MSCI
MSCI 627.title: Marine Phytoplankton

MSCI 706.description: Application of the principles of ecology with the methods of engineering to design sustainable ecosystems to better integrate human society with the coastal environment.
MSCI 706.subject: MSCI
MSCI 706.title: Coastal Nature-Based Solutions

MSCI 709.description: This course provides a hands-on, project-oriented investigation of current approaches for research in marine science, ecology and environmental science. Components of the course will include exploratory data analyses, statistics, graphics and the R programming language. Prior programming experience is beneficial, but not required.
MSCI 709.subject: MSCI
MSCI 709.title: Marine Data Science with R

MSCI 711.description: An overview of Earth’s climate history during Cenozoic. Emphasis will be placed on Pleistocene glacial-interglacial climate variability and understanding the proxies used to reconstruct past climate changes.
MSCI 711.subject: MSCI
MSCI 711.title: Paleoclimatology

MSCI 716.description: Relationship of sequence stratigraphy to sea level variations, tectonics and sedimentation. Construction and analyses of paleogeographic maps, regional cross-sections, and chronostratigraphic charts.
MSCI 716.subject: MSCI
MSCI 716.title: Eustasy and Global Variations in Sequence Stratigraphy

MSCI 717.description: Sources, transport, and fate of organic matter in natural environments including soils, riverine, estuarine, coastal and open ocean sediments and waters.
MSCI 717.subject: MSCI
MSCI 717.title: Organic Geochemistry

MSCI 745.description: A comprehensive study of the origin and development of the major structural features of the ocean basins and the continental margins. Discussion of the techniques used in obtaining geologic data and the interpretation of sedimentary processes, vulcanism, and the stratigraphy of the ocean basins.
MSCI 745.subject: MSCI
MSCI 745.title: Geological Oceanography

MSCI 752.description: Biological, geological, and physical processes that influence the cyling of major bioactive elements (C, O, N, P, S) in marine waters and sediments.
MSCI 752.subject: MSCI
MSCI 752.title: Marine Biogeochemistry

MSCI 755.description: Explores the intersection between conservation and environmental health with a particular focus on coastal and marine case studies.
MSCI 755.subject: MSCI
MSCI 755.title: Marine Conservation and Environmental Health

MSCI 767.description: Concepts in systems ecology and ecological modeling. Emphasis on the use of models and computer simulations in examining environmental interactions, predicting environmental impact, and facilitating the process of environmental planning. Lab practice in model development and computer simulation analysis.
MSCI 767.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: MATH 111 or equivalent, ecology, ENHS 660.
MSCI 767.subject: MSCI
MSCI 767.title: Ecological Modeling and Environmental Planning

MSCI 769.description: Theoretical aspects and examples of the variety of reproductive and life history patterns found in animals and plants as adaptations to various environmental constraints. Three lecture hours per week.
MSCI 769.subject: MSCI
MSCI 769.title: Reproductive Ecology

MSCI 777.description: Primarily for teachers. Marine science materials with emphasis on coastal environments. Field exercises.
MSCI 777.subject: MSCI
MSCI 777.title: Current Topics in Marine Ecology for Teachers

MSCI 778.description: Primarily for teachers. Marine science materials with emphasis on coastal environments. Field exercises.
MSCI 778.subject: MSCI
MSCI 778.title: Current Topics in Marine Ecology for Teachers

MSCI 781.description: Geographic and hydrodynamic aspects of oceanography, with emphasis on estuaries. Physical properties of sea water and theories and methods involved in ocean currents, air-sea interaction, waves, and tides.
MSCI 781.subject: MSCI
MSCI 781.title: Physical Oceanography

MSCI 782.description: Chemical characteristics of sea water, distribution of properties, and chemical processes in the oceans, with emphasis on estuaries.
MSCI 782.subject: MSCI
MSCI 782.title: Chemical Oceanography

MSCI 783.description: Techniques in the analysis of oceanographic data sequences, including filtering techniques, fast Fourier transformers, and empirical orthogonal functions.
MSCI 783.subject: MSCI
MSCI 783.title: Oceanographic Time Series Analysis

MSCI 784.description: Equations governing the large-scale dynamics of the atmosphere and ocean, rotational influence, shallow water equations, vorticity, quasi-geostrophic dynamics, Rossby waves, energy and enstrophy, and geostrophic turbulence.
MSCI 784.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: MATH 241 or ECIV 360 or GEOL 582/MSCI 582 or GEOL 781/MSCI 781.
MSCI 784.subject: MSCI
MSCI 784.title: Geophysical Fluid Dynamics

MSCI 785.description: Elementary applications of the basic equations, scale analysis, planetary boundary layer, atmospheric oscillations, synoptic and mesoscale systems, hydrodynamic instability, cyclogenesis, frontogenesis, energy cycle, momentum budget, and tropical motion systems.
MSCI 785.subject: MSCI
MSCI 785.title: Atmospheric Dynamics

MSCI 790.description: Directed research topics to be individually assigned and supervised by graduate faculty.
MSCI 790.subject: MSCI
MSCI 790.title: Directed Individual Studies in Marine Sciences

MSCI 795.description: Problems associated with coastal population growth and development. Emphasis is on the working group approach to ameliorating impacts on ecosystem and human health.
MSCI 795.subject: MSCI
MSCI 795.title: Issues in Coastal Environmental Health

MSCI 798.description: In depth research methods and techniques in preparation of thesis or dissertation.
MSCI 798.subject: MSCI
MSCI 798.title: Research in Marine Science

MSCI 800.description: Advanced topics in geoscience research presented in departmental seminar format. Contains a mix of marine science, geological science, and environmental science content.
MSCI 800.subject: MSCI
MSCI 800.title: Marine Science Seminar
